title.en: OpenAI API Basics: Your First AI-Powered App
title.ta: OpenAI API அடிப்படைகள்: உங்கள் முதல் AI-இயக்கும் செயலி

description.en: Learn to use the OpenAI API — set up API keys, make chat completions, and stream responses in real-time.
description.ta: OpenAI API பயன்படுத்தக் கற்றுக்கொள்ளுங்கள் — API keys அமைத்தல், chat completions செய்தல், நிகழ்நேர streaming.

story_variants.en:
## Vaathiyaar's First API Call

Vaathiyaar opens a terminal. "Students, until now we've been talking ABOUT AI. Today, we BUILD with it. One API call is all it takes to add intelligence to any Python program."

### Setting Up

1. Get your API key from [platform.openai.com](https://platform.openai.com)
2. Store it safely: `export OPENAI_API_KEY='sk-...'`
3. Install the library: `pip install openai`

### The Chat Completions API

Every OpenAI call uses the **messages** pattern:
- `system` — Sets AI behavior
- `user` — Your input
- `assistant` — AI's previous responses (for multi-turn)

### Streaming

For long responses, **streaming** shows tokens as they're generated:
```python
for chunk in stream:
    print(chunk.choices[0].delta.content, end='')
```

> **Key Insight:** The OpenAI API is stateless — it doesn't remember previous calls. You must send the full conversation history each time.
story_variants.ta:
## வாத்தியாரின் முதல் API அழைப்பு

வாத்தியார் ஒரு terminal-ஐ திறக்கிறார். "மாணவர்களே, இதுவரை நாம் AI பற்றி பேசிக்கொண்டிருந்தோம். இன்று, அதைக் கொண்டு உருவாக்குகிறோம்."

explanation.en: Import os to access environment variables for the API key
Initialize the client — it automatically reads OPENAI_API_KEY from environment

steps.line: client = OpenAI()  # reads OPENAI_API_KEY from env

explanation.en: Create the client — never hardcode your API key in source code
Now let's make our first chat completion
The chat completions endpoint is the primary way to interact with GPT models
Call the chat completions API — this sends your messages to the model
gpt-4o-mini is fast, cheap ($0.15/1M input tokens), and great for most tasks
Messages is a list of conversation turns
System message sets the AI's personality and constraints
User message is your actual question or request
Limit response to 200 tokens to keep it concise
API call is made — response is returned

output: A list comprehension is a concise way to create lists in Python
using a single line of code. Instead of writing a for loop to
append items to a list, you write [expression for item in iterable].

animation_sequence.code:
from openai import OpenAI
client = OpenAI()

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model='gpt-4o-mini',
    messages=[
        {'role':'system','content':'You are a helpful assistant.'},
        {'role':'user','content':'What is Python in one sentence?'}
    ],
    max_tokens=50, temperature=0.7
)

answer = response.choices[0].message.content
print(answer)
print(f'Tokens used: {response.usage.total_tokens}')

executionSteps.explanation: Chat completions — the main API endpoint
max_tokens limits length, temperature controls creativity

executionSteps.output: Python is a versatile programming language.

instruction.en: The sandbox has no network or API key, so the starter code provides `FakeOpenAI`, an offline stand-in that accepts the same `client.chat.completions.create(...)` arguments as the real SDK and returns the same response shape. 1) Complete `make_client(env)`: return None when 'OPENAI_API_KEY' is missing from the env dict, otherwise `FakeOpenAI(api_key=...)`. 2) Complete `ask(client, question)`: call `client.chat.completions.create` with a model name and a messages list holding a 'system' message (the assistant's role) followed by a 'user' message with the question; return a tuple `(answer_text, total_tokens)`.
instruction.ta: Sandbox-ல் network-உம் API key-உம் இல்லை, எனவே starter code-ல் `FakeOpenAI` உள்ளது: இது உண்மையான SDK போலவே `client.chat.completions.create(...)` arguments-ஐ ஏற்று, அதே வடிவிலான response-ஐத் தரும் offline மாற்று. 1) `make_client(env)`-ஐ நிறைவு செய்யுங்கள்: env dict-ல் 'OPENAI_API_KEY' இல்லையென்றால் None, இருந்தால் `FakeOpenAI(api_key=...)` திருப்புங்கள். 2) `ask(client, question)`-ஐ நிறைவு செய்யுங்கள்: model பெயர் மற்றும் ஒரு 'system' message (assistant-இன் பங்கு), அதைத் தொடர்ந்து கேள்வியுடன் ஒரு 'user' message கொண்ட messages list உடன் `client.chat.completions.create`-ஐ அழைத்து, `(answer_text, total_tokens)` tuple-ஐத் திருப்புங்கள்.

practice_challenges.test_code:
assert make_client({}) is None, "make_client must return None when OPENAI_API_KEY is missing"
_c = make_client({"OPENAI_API_KEY": "sk-test"})
assert isinstance(_c, FakeOpenAI), "make_client must return FakeOpenAI(api_key=...) when the key is set"
_res = ask(_c, "What is a list?")
assert isinstance(_res, tuple) and len(_res) == 2, "ask must return a tuple (answer_text, total_tokens)"
_req = _c.chat.completions.last_request
assert _req is not None, "ask must call client.chat.completions.create(...)"
assert isinstance(_req["model"], str) and _req["model"], "pass a model name, e.g. model='gpt-4o-mini'"
_msgs = _req["messages"]
assert len(_msgs) >= 2 and _msgs[0]["role"] == "system", "the first message must be the 'system' message"
assert _msgs[-1]["role"] == "user" and "What is a list?" in _msgs[-1]["content"], "the last message must be a 'user' message containing the question"
assert _res[0] == "Here are 3 Python tips: use f-strings, read error messages carefully, practise every day.", "the answer text is response.choices[0].message.content"
_expected_total = sum(len(m["content"].split()) for m in _msgs) + len(_res[0].split())
assert _res[1] == _expected_total, "total_tokens must come from response.usage.total_tokens"
print("All OpenAI client tests passed!")
